Standard errors and confidence intervals for conductance parameters

Source: R/inference.R
terradish_inference.Rd

vcov() and confint() report the uncertainty of the fitted conductance parameters from the curvature (observed information) of the log-likelihood at the estimate. They work on a full or slim fit.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted terradish object.

...

Unused arguments for generic compatibility.

parm

Names or indices of parameters to include.

level

Confidence level between zero and one. This is the quantity that summary() calls conf.level and that conductance() and plot() call quantile.

Value

vcov() returns the named covariance matrix of the conductance parameters, the inverse of the observed information, on the scale of coef(). confint() returns a matrix with one row per parameter and two columns holding the lower and upper Wald limits, labeled by their percentiles. nobs() returns the number of focal sites.

Details

Reading the output. Both functions are on the scale of coef(): log conductance per unit of each covariate (per standard deviation for covariates scaled with scale_covariates), and map units for Gaussian sigma.<layer> smoothing scales. confint() returns Wald intervals, the estimate plus or minus a normal quantile times its standard error. sqrt(diag(vcov(fit))) gives the standard errors that summary() prints. Exponentiate a log-conductance estimate or interval endpoint to read it as a conductance multiplier: exp(confint(fit)) is the interval for the ratio of conductance per unit increase in the covariate, and an interval that excludes 1 on that scale excludes zero on the log scale. Do not exponentiate rows for Gaussian smoothing scales.

The intervals are conditional on the fitted model. For Wishart fits they also depend on the supplied nu: standard errors scale as 1 / sqrt(nu) (see terradish_rescale_nu). Uncertainty in the nuisance parameters is reported separately by summary().

Gaussian scale intervals are Wald intervals truncated at the fitted bounds. Stored profile intervals take precedence when their confidence level matches. The observation count is the number of focal sites (individuals or populations), the sample size that AICc and BIC use in aic_table. Pairwise observations are not counted, because pairs that share a site are not independent.

See also

terradish, slim_terradish, gaussian_scale_profile, terradish_rescale_nu

Other inference and model comparison: aic_table(), mlpe_response_change(), terradish_cv_folds(), terradish_folds(), terradish_ibe_ratio(), terradish_rescale_nu()

Examples

# A small model-based example, with fixed information supplied explicitly.
r <- terra::rast(nrows = 8, ncols = 8, xmin = 0, xmax = 8, ymin = 0, ymax = 8)
terra::values(r) <- sin(seq_len(64) / 5) + seq_len(64) / 64
names(r) <- "x"
sites <- terra::xyFromCell(r, c(1, 8, 20, 37, 57, 64))
graph <- conductance_surface(r, sites)
simulated <- simulate_covariance_response(c(x = 0.6), ~x, graph,
                                          nu = 1000, seed = 93)
response <- simulated$covariance
fit <- terradish(response ~ x, graph, measurement_model = wishart_covariance,
                 nu = 1000)
coef(fit)       # Relative log conductance per unit of x.
#>         x 
#> 0.6761321 
vcov(fit)       # Joint uncertainty in conductance parameters.
#>             x
#> x 0.007999916
confint(fit)    # A model-based interval conditional on the supplied nu.
#>       2.5 %    97.5 %
#> x 0.5008285 0.8514357
exp(confint(fit))  # The same interval as a conductance multiplier.
#>      2.5 %   97.5 %
#> x 1.650088 2.343008
nobs(fit)       # Number of focal sites, the sample size for AICc and BIC.
#> [1] 6
